 Order
The present petition is filed by the petitioners- accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR in Crime No.212/2021 registered by Holehonnur police arising out of the PCR No.38/2021 referred by the Magistrate for the offences punishable under Sections 181, 182, 418,
420, 465, 468, 471, 474, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC. 
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2. 
3. The case of the prosecution is that on the private complaint filed by respondent No.2, the Magistrate referred the matter to the police, in turn, the police registered the FIR in Crime No.212/2021. The allegation NC: 2024:KHC:12318 against the petitioners is that though respondent No.2, the petitioner's father and their sons, apart from Mallamma and Malleshappa are the legal heirs of Mudigowda, the petitioners have created the false geological tree and produced before the Authority and got transferred. The Joint Family property belongs to Mudigowda only with trusted two properties. Therefore, complainant- respondent No.2 prayed for taking action. 
4. The complainant said to be filed the complaint before the police, but they did not entertain. 
Hence, he has filed the private complaint before the Magistrate under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., which is under challenge. 
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent No.2 has not followed the procedure or guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA AND ANOTHER vs. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287. He did not file the complaint before the police, and subsequently, if the complaint is not NC:
2024:KHC:12318 registered, he may approach the Superintendent of police under Section 154(3) of Cr.P.C. Thereafter, he has to file the complaint along with the swearing affidavit for approaching all the authorities, which is not filed, and it is shown in the index sheet that there is no affidavit along with the complaint. Hence, he prays for allowing the petition. 
6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 objected to the petition and contended that respondent No.2 approached the police but the police refused to register the FIR. Therefore, he approached the Magistrate and the Magistrate has referred the complaint to the police for registering the FIR. The petitioners are required for investigation. Whereas the other family members are left out in the partition. Respondent No.2 also filed a suit for partition which is pending before the Civil Court. Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition. 
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the materials on record. 
NC: 2024:KHC:12318 8. A perusal of the material on record would indicate that respondent No.2 has filed a civil suit in OS.No.46/2020. The main contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the civil suit Sri. M.P Aravinda vs State Of Karnataka on 25 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82199702/
3 has already seized the matter and the question of filing the complaint does not arise. Apart from that, while filing the complaint, respondent No.2 has not followed the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA (supra). 
9. On perusal of the complaint at paragraph 8, respondent No.2 has stated that he approached the Superintend of Police, Shivamogga as well as the Jurisdictional Rural Police Bhadravati on 09.07.2020 and 10.07.2020 respectively but they have not registered the FIR. Therefore, he approached the Magistrate. However, respondent No.2 has not filed an affidavit in this regard except for the for the verification endorsement made in the complaint itself. 
NC: 2024:KHC:12318 10. On perusal of the same, the complaint was filed against the petitioners before the Bhadravathi Rural Police as well as the Superintendent of police on 09.07.2020 and 10.07.2020 as there is no affidavit. Therefore, the reference itself is not in accordance with law as per the conditions imposed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA (supra). On this ground, the criminal proceedings against the petitioners is not sustainable. The reference of the complaint to the police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. and registering the FIR are hereby quashed. 
11. Liberty is reserved to respondent No.2 to initiate the proceedings against the petitioners in accordance with law. 
Accordingly, the petition is disposed off. 
Sd/-
